labelChirho: Ezion-geber (port city on the Gulf of Aqaba)
descriptionChirho: The proper noun עֶצְיוֹן גֶּבֶר designating the ancient port city of Ezion-geber, located at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba (modern-day Eilat area), known as a station during Israel's wilderness wandering (Num 33:35-36, Deut 2:8) and later as Solomon's shipbuilding port (1 Kgs 9:26, 22:48; 2 Chr 8:17, 20:36). All three clusters are the same toponym with different prepositional contexts. Multilingual evidence: English 'Ezion-geber/Etsyon-Gever,' Spanish 'Ezión Geber/Etsión Géber,' Hindi एस्योन गेबेर, Arabic عَصْيُونَ جَابَرَ / عِصيُونَ جابَرَ (consistent transliteration), Korean 에시온 게보르/에치온 게버, Swahili Esion Geberi/Ezion Geberi. Locative, directional, and conjunctive-separative uses are purely syntactic.
